text: This chapter closes by tying everything back to where this catalog already left you: Data Governance Foundations and Data Quality Management.

Data Governance Foundations gave you decision rights, accountability, owners, stewards, and councils. Data Quality Management gave you concrete dimensions for judging whether data is good enough — accuracy, completeness, consistency, validity, uniqueness, timeliness. Neither gets thrown out here. Both get extended.

Data owners and stewards still own the datasets feeding a model — AI governance adds model owners on top, it doesn't replace them. Existing classification and handling standards still apply. And the same six quality dimensions still define good data — Lesson 8 applies them specifically to training data.

Three things without a direct equivalent in plain data governance. The model itself as a new kind of asset that acts continuously once deployed. Training-specific concerns like provenance, consent, and labeling, because this data gets baked into permanent behavior. And production monitoring for drift, since nobody corrects a model's behavior just by noticing a bad report.

An organization that tries to do AI governance without working data governance first ends up approving a model's fairness testing while nobody can say where its training data even came from. The foundation has to hold before the layer on top of it means anything.
Next chapter: Data for AI — starting with how training data itself gets governed, provenance, consent, quality, bias, labeling, and synthetic data.
